audit.why: Rumble 46.94% over 948 games — an unfavoured lane. Rumble owns levels 1-2 on raw range, Irelia takes 4-6 once Bladesurge has reset targets and Flawless Duet is up, and the side lane is hers at two items. The existing chart already reads that way.
Spikes are placed correctly: Rumble at 1-2, Irelia at 3-5, Rumble's R at 6, Irelia's Blade of the Ruined King first item. Nothing needed moving, only the mechanical reasons attached to each.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is never mentioned, and the 'late' text credits her with a 'W passive block' that eats Rumble's damage.
audit.why: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage taken while she charges. Rumble's entire kit — Flamespitter, Electro Harpoon, The Equalizer — is magic damage, so her one defensive cooldown does nothing against you. That is the single most decisive interaction in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: State plainly that Defiant Dance cuts physical only and burn through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text says she needs 'four passive stacks' to dash on you and that her passive gives 'armor shred'.
audit.why: Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — no armour shred, and it has nothing to do with Bladesurge. Bladesurge refunds its cooldown when the target is Marked or dies; Marks come from Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge. Tracking stacks to predict her dash is advice that will get a player killed.
audit.corrected: Track killable minions and her Flawless Duet, not passive stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'E-stun you mid-Flamespitter channel' implies the stun cancels Flamespitter.
audit.why: Flamespitter is not a channel — it burns in a cone for 3 seconds regardless. The stun's real cost is that you cannot turn or reposition the cone, so it expires on empty air.
audit.corrected: Reframed around cone control rather than an interrupt that does not happen.

audit.why: Bladesurge heals on every cast and reset, which is what makes her extended trades win; Grievous Wounds timing decides them.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into the late-game line.

edits.before: Irelia's full kit (Q-reset chains + E-stun) lets her gap-close through Flamespitter and punish any Overheat window instantly.
edits.after: Flawless Duet stuns from 850 and Marks you, refunding Bladesurge — that chain, not passive stacks, walks her through Flamespitter.

edits.before: Stack four passive stacks on the wave then Q-dash through minions onto you when Scrap Shield is on cooldown
edits.after: Chain Bladesurge off dying minions onto you the moment Scrap Shield is down — the reset is her entire gap-close

edits.before: E-stun you mid-Flamespitter channel to end the sustained-damage trade before you get full Danger Zone value
edits.after: Flawless Duet-stun you so you cannot turn the Flamespitter cone and its 3 seconds burn on empty ground

edits.before: Use Equalizer across the river or at a chokepoint to punish her disengaging or to deter an all-in you cannot win cleanly 1v1
edits.after: Use The Equalizer across the river or a chokepoint to punish her disengage, or to deter an all-in you cannot win cleanly 1v1

edits.before: Irelia's E-stun chains into Q-resets and her passive armor shred means she wins every extended trade if she can close — deny minion assists by waving slowly at your tower.
edits.after: Flawless Duet Marks you, and a Marked target refunds Bladesurge, so one stun becomes a second free dash — deny the reset targets by holding the wave slow near your tower.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are where this lane turns against you. Irelia's Q-reset chain through the wave means she can close the distance through your Flamespitter cone and land the E-stun before you finish trading, cutting your sustained damage window in half. Your gameplan is to keep the wave at your tower so she must walk up without minion assists — denied resets means she is just a melee champion walking into Flamespitter range. Track her passive stacks: below four stacks she cannot dash onto you safely. At Level 6 your Equalizer changes the dynamic — you do not need to win the 1v1 to win the lane. Drop the rocket wall perpendicular to her likely dash path and she burns for free, or use it to deny a gank setup when she shoves and overextends.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are where this lane turns against you. Bladesurge refunds itself on a dying or Marked target, so a full wave is a ladder she climbs through your Flamespitter cone to land Flawless Duet before your three seconds are up. Keep the wave at your tower and those reset targets vanish — denied resets, she is only a melee champion walking into your cone. Defiant Dance reduces physical damage only, so her one defensive button does nothing to any part of your kit: burn straight through the charge instead of backing off it. At Level 6 The Equalizer changes the dynamic — you do not need to win the 1v1 to win the lane. Drop the wall perpendicular to her dash path and she burns for free, or use it on an overextended shove.

edits.before: By first item she is building Blade of the Ruined King, and the percent-HP shred bypasses your Scrap Shield and outraces your Flamespitter DoT in extended trades. You are no longer trading favorably 1v1 — accept that and lean into Equalizer teamfighting instead. Your cross-map ultimate is one of the best in the game at this stage: land it in a choke, Dragon pit, or Baron approach and you win teamfights she cannot even reach. If the game reaches two-plus items and she is ahead, do not attempt the side-lane duel — your Danger Zone burst is frontloaded and her W passive block plus BotRK sustain will eat through it. Play the teamfight mage role and let Equalizer be the reason your team wins while she is distracted in a side lane.
edits.after: By first item she is building Blade of the Ruined King, and the percent-HP shred chews through Scrap Shield and outraces your Flamespitter DoT in extended trades. You are no longer trading favourably 1v1 — accept that and lean into The Equalizer instead. Your cross-map ultimate is one of the best in the game at this stage: land it in a choke, Dragon pit, or Baron approach and you win fights she cannot reach. If she is ahead at two items, refuse the side-lane duel — your Danger Zone damage is frontloaded and every Bladesurge reset heals her straight back through it, so buy Oblivion Orb before you even consider standing there. Let the rockets, not the duel, be the reason your team wins.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — Her engage CC. E-slow it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Flawless Duet 16s at rank 1: her engage CC and the Mark that refunds Bladesurge — E-slow it. - Bladesurge resets on Marked or dying targets, so count minions. - The Equalizer: kill windows only.

notes: Two fabricated mechanics removed: Irelia's passive does not grant armour shred and does not gate her dash at 'four stacks' (Ionian Fervor is attack speed plus on-hit at max stacks; Bladesurge resets on Marked or dying targets). The highest-value addition is that Defiant Dance reduces physical damage only, so it is worthless against Rumble's all-magic kit — it was completely absent from the page. Also fixed: Flamespitter is not a channel, so her stun does not cancel it. Rumble kit-file flags 'knockup'/'terrain' on Scrap Shield contradict Riot's description and were not used.
